root_idea.summary: The root centers on greenness, verdure, and the color green.
root_idea.development: The color term extends to dark, dusky, or blackish hues because luxuriant, moisture-rich vegetation can appear dark from a distance. Related developments include freshness, tenderness, verdure, abundance, and several idiomatic uses.

qac_form_accounting.reason: خُضْر is explicitly identified as the plural of أَخْضَر and is best represented under the singular adjective citation form.

senses.definition: Green; of the green color, including green-colored objects or garments.
senses.usage_conditions: The plural خُضْر is used substantivally or adjectivally for multiple green things. In Arabic color terminology, intense greenness may shade toward a dark or blackish appearance.

senses.definition: Green or verdant, having become green.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic feminine form مُخْضَرَّة describes the earth as green and verdant, with greenness associated with moisture and growing vegetation.

senses.definition: Green vegetation; a green plant, or green branch.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is substantival and refers to green plant growth produced from the rain.

senses.definition: Verdant or rich in vegetation, especially of a place or land.
senses.usage_conditions: A reported Quranic reading applies the feminine form to verdant land; the historical citation is not converted here into a modern verse location.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make or render something green.
In a tropical idiom, to bless or prosper someone in an art, trade, traffic, or means of subsistence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions describing a person as blessed in a particular livelihood and therefore advised to remain with it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sell fruits before their goodness or soundness has become apparent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction concerns a prohibited or disapproved sale of fruit before ripeness or reliable quality is manifest.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of moisture: to make seed-produce soft or tender.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject is the moisture affecting the produce.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut green herbage, a tree, or green branches; also to cut a thing off entirely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source includes cutting herbage while still green and the idiomatic cutting off of a thing such as a nose.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To die young, in one's fresh and flourishing state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a figurative passive use derived from being cut while still fresh.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To eat fruit while it is green or unripe.
To deflower; in a specified use, to have sexual intercourse before the partner has reached puberty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of taking something before its proper maturity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take an untrained, refractory camel, attach its nose-rein, and drive it.
To take up a load or burden.
To become dark, blackish, or dusky; to take on a green-black hue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of colors, night, darkness, and other things whose intense or mixed hue is described through the traditional association between green and black.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter a state of plenty or prosperity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical expression describes the skin as becoming green from carrying the produce of one's land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of seed-produce: to become soft or tender.
Of herbage: to be cut.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a separately reported use of the Form IX expression, with a possible passive interpretation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fresh green herbage, tender trees or branches, and herbs in the first stage of growth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The terms can denote herbage that is fresh-cut, soft, or still early in its growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fresh, juicy, delicate, pleasant, or enjoyable in idiomatic expressions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The idioms may describe an acquisition as obtained without payment or in a fresh state, worldly goods as delicate and pleasant, or warfare as fresh and loved because of its victory and spoil.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unrevenged or unexpiated, of blood that has gone without retaliation or compensation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression for blood that has gone unavenged; the accompanying word is an imitative sequent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A green palm branch, with or without its leaves.
Greenness, verdure, or the green color; also a dark, ashy, tawny, or blackish hue in traditional color terminology.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The color term may be applied to plants, animals, people, water, garments, and other things; its exact shade varies by object and context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Softness, tenderness, freshness, juiciness, or pleasant edibility of produce.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an abstract and descriptive extension of the condition of fresh, tender vegetation or produce.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A palm tree bearing good green dates; also a kind of admired green date resembling glass.
Milk mixed with a large quantity of water, becoming dark or ashy in color.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may refer to fresh or stored milk diluted approximately to one part milk and two parts water, according to one explanation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sea.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical or proper-name use motivated by the sea's described green appearance; it is treated as a separate lexical use from ordinary greenness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A palm tree whose dates fall while still unripe and green.
A woman who scarcely ever completes a pregnancy and casts its product.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical lexical use of the diminutive form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular green or dark-ashy bird, also called the akhyal or qāriya in the reported descriptions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources differ over whether the bird was regarded as a good or evil omen.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The shrub or tree called رِمْث when it has grown tall.
A particular green herb or plant, including a rough leguminous herb and another named plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The descriptions distinguish these plants from slender, succulent herbs and identify some as deep-rooted pasture plants.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In extended descriptive and idiomatic uses: tawny, brownish, blackish, or black; of pure Arab lineage when describing skin; and, in one expression, a young man whose facial hair has begun to grow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are conventional extensions of the color term and do not replace the ordinary Quranic sense 'green'.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Green herbs, leguminous plants, or fresh fruits and herbs, used substantivally.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form appears in expressions concerning produce and its treatment, including a reported statement about alms-tax on such produce.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A beautiful woman of bad or corrupt origin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional figurative expression comparing attractive growth in polluted dung to beauty arising from a bad upbringing or lineage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sky or heaven.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical substantival use motivated by its apparent greenness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bucket that has become green or blackish from long use in drawing water.
The gathered body, mass, stock, or origin of a people; by extension, their worldly life, prosperity, plenty, or enjoyment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in an idiom for the collective strength or prosperity of a group. One reported reading instead derives the expression from another root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Domestic pigeons.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is explained by their predominant ash or greenish coloration even though individual birds may be variously colored.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Gold, flesh-meat, and wine, used as a collective plural expression.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical substantival use of the plural of أَخْضَرُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fresh or recent; also soft or tender when applied to herbage or produce.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The abstract adjective can describe a recent affair or fresh affection, as well as tender vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A soft, comfortable, plentiful, and pleasant mode of life.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical expression for ease and abundance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of a particular star or asterism associated with one of the rainy-season anwāʾ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The astronomical identification is reported approximately and is distinct from the color adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Cantharides, a green or dark-ashy medicinal fly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A diminutive lexicalized name for the insect, whose medical properties are treated in pharmacological works.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular disease of the eye.

cautions: The classical color range of أَخْضَر and خُضْر can include dark, dusky, or blackish shades; this does not erase the ordinary Quranic color sense 'green'.
A historical Lane Quran citation reported as 'xxii. 62' is not converted into a modern verse location here.
